narrative_prose: Silas braced himself against the brass railing, his boots vibrating with the low, resonant hum of the magnetohydrodynamic engines. Below, the ferrofluid sea caught the dawn light, its surface a chaotic dance of glittering metallic ripples driven by a violent Kelvin-Helmholtz shear. The smell of ozone and hot oil was thick in the air, carrying a faint metallic tang that coated the back of his throat. He reached for the heavy brass control valves, knowing that if the magnetic containment field faltered even a fraction, the resulting wave could breach the primary deck lip. Beside him, Hector grinned, already reaching for the overheating copper coils with reckless enthusiasm. Silas sighed, releasing his grip on the main valve and stepping back, nodding for the prodigy to take the lead.
